summary: 67-year-old man with 10 weeks of looser stools, dark blood mixed with stool, 4 kg weight loss, iron-deficiency anaemia (Hb 10.2, ferritin 9) and FIT 186 µg Hb/g: suspected colorectal cancer pathway (colonoscopy) under NICE NG12/DG56.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Change in bowel habit with blood in the stool
inputs.hpi: Ten weeks of looser stools, 3–4 a day (previously once daily), with intermittent dark red blood mixed in. Lost 4 kg without trying. More tired and breathless on the stairs. No abdominal pain. GP FIT result 186 µg Hb/g. No previous colonoscopy. No family history of bowel cancer. Type 2 diabetes on metformin.

exam.abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no palpable mass, no hepatomegaly.
exam.other: PR: no palpable mass; dark blood on the glove.

inputs.socialHistory: Retired civil servant. Ex-smoker (20 pack-years). 10 units alcohol a week.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected colorectal cancer
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected colorectal cancer: change in bowel habit, rectal bleeding, weight loss, iron-deficiency anaemia, FIT 186 µg Hb/g. Urgent colonoscopy on the suspected cancer pathway.

emergencyLevel.note: Suspected cancer pathway: seen within 2 weeks. "priority" or above.

redFlags.note: The triage cancer screen (NG12 criteria) should trigger: age ≥ 60 with change in bowel habit, IDA, rectal bleeding.
FIT ≥ 10 µg Hb/g is the NICE DG56 threshold for a suspected cancer referral; the result should be read and surfaced.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — suspected cancer: recognition and referral (lower gastrointestinal tract cancers)
guideline.section: Lower GI (updated 2023): refer on the suspected cancer pathway if FIT ≥ 10 µg Hb/g; offer FIT to adults with symptoms such as change in bowel habit, IDA, weight loss
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (NG12). First published 2015; lower GI recommendations updated 2023 to incorporate DG56.

guideline.name: NICE DG56 — quantitative FIT to guide colorectal cancer pathway referral in primary care
guideline.section: FIT threshold 10 µg Hb/g faeces for suspected colorectal cancer referral
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Quantitative faecal immunochemical testing to guide colorectal cancer pathway referral in primary care (DG56). 2023.

guideline.name: ACPGBI/BSG joint guideline — FIT in patients with signs or symptoms of suspected colorectal cancer
guideline.section: Symptomatic FIT ≥ 10 µg Hb/g → urgent colorectal investigation (colonoscopy or CT colonography)
guideline.citation: Monahan KJ, Davies MM, Abulafi M, et al. Faecal immunochemical testing (FIT) in patients with signs or symptoms of suspected colorectal cancer (CRC): a joint guideline from the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland (ACPGBI) and the British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG). Gut. 2022;71:1939–1962.

guideline.name: BSG guideline — management of iron deficiency anaemia in adults
guideline.citation: Snook J, Bhala N, Beales ILP, et al. British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for the management of iron deficiency anaemia in adults. Gut. 2021;70:2030–2051.

rationale: Base case for the colorectal-cancer red flags: every NG12 feature is present (age ≥ 60, CIBH, rectal bleeding, weight loss, IDA) plus a FIT well above 10 µg Hb/g. If this does not reach the suspected cancer pathway, nothing will. Pairs with rectal-bleeding-young-haemorrhoidal.
